# Amy Wu Coaching & Advisory

> Executive coaching for engineers and engineering leaders building resilient careers in the AI era.

## Who

Amy Wu — also known as Amy (Chencheng) Wu; her LinkedIn and Substack byline read
Chencheng Wu. She is one person: coach, advisor, and AI builder, formerly an
Engineering Director at LinkedIn and Instacart across roughly 15 years and five
promotions, from IC through Director leading 50+ engineers. Certified Master
of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (MNLP), iNLP Center. She now coaches senior
technology leaders and advises organizations on AI adoption, while building
inside an early-stage startup.

- Website: https://amywucoaching.com/
- About: https://amywucoaching.com/about/
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/chenchengwu/
- Newsletter (Substack): https://newsletter.amywucoaching.com/
- Full essay archive on this site: https://amywucoaching.com/newsletter/

## What she does

Coaching for engineers and engineering leaders — senior ICs, engineering
managers, and directors, mostly in big tech — keeping their footing through
reorgs, new managers, new companies, and acquisitions, while building toward what
comes next on their own terms: relocation, a side project that becomes a
business, a career that doesn't depend on one employer. Topics include rating and
calibration, the IC-versus-management question, influence without authority, and
leading through AI transformation.

The framework she teaches is **MOAT** — Make, Outlook, Audience, Tribe — four
dimensions of a career that compounds rather than one that only climbs.
Engagements: The Next Move (choosing the next role by working backward from
where you want to end up, then landing the offer); Navigate the Org (influence
inside your current org); and Scale the Team,
ongoing advisory for first-time managers, engineering leaders, and founders whose
teams are growing fast (org design, delegation, first managers, how work splits
between people and AI; not outsourced management).
See https://amywucoaching.com/services/.

## Signature series: The AI-Native Leader

https://amywucoaching.com/ai-native-leader/

- [AI doesn't need fewer managers. It needs system thinkers.](https://amywucoaching.com/newsletter/the-ai-native-manager-part-1-the/) — The question isn't whether to be an IC or a manager. It's whether you can design the system the work runs on.
- [Stop looking for the playbook. Start building the harness.](https://amywucoaching.com/newsletter/the-ai-native-leader-part-2-stop/) — Nobody has an AI adoption playbook that works, because a playbook is the wrong artifact. What you need is a harness.
- [It's not about switching chairs.](https://amywucoaching.com/newsletter/the-ai-native-leader-part-3-what/) — The conventional org has many layers. The AI-native one has two patterns of work — and neither is gated by a title.
- [Invest ahead of the rubric.](https://amywucoaching.com/newsletter/the-ai-native-leader-part-4-invest/) — The work has already changed. The promotion rubric hasn't. Waiting for it to catch up is the expensive choice.

Core claim: AI is not removing management from engineering organizations. It is
removing the coordination overhead that disguised what management actually was —
system design, defining what good looks like, deciding what gets built. In an
AI-native org, influence follows whoever does that well, regardless of title.
